title: T5 hallway: the door registry
purpose: Every door in the hallway: what question it answers, where it is, and how fresh it is. A door is a documented, versioned, reachable entry point onto one part of the program. This registry exists because the design names a hallway whose job is navigation, and a hallway with no door inventory is a corridor.
why_a_registry_and_not_a_list: The design record already carried a ten-row door table by hand, and within one session that table's own category grew: two more doors were demanded by the design, and seven more were built for the retrieval, spec and gate work. Hand-maintained tables do not survive that. Worse, the design's own audit found a reader-facing document disagreeing with three separately-asserted implementations, and a stale Heartbeat size that the code comments already said was fixed. Documentation drift here is not cosmetic, so freshness is CHECKED by tools/door_lint.py rather than asserted.

state_legend.CURRENT: Verified against the code it describes.
state_legend.PARTLY_FIXED: Some claims verified, some known wrong. Treat the wrong parts as absent.
state_legend.STALE: Known not to match the code. Read only for what is uniquely valuable in it.
state_legend.SUPERSEDED: Replaced, but retained because it uniquely holds something nothing else does.
state_legend.BUILT: Created 2026-09-30 as part of the retrieval and spec work.

doors.question: What is actually installed versus proposed
doors.notes: PyO3, CBOR, serde_json and pydantic are ABSENT. watchdog is NOT installed, which is why the live hook falls back to polling.

doors.question: What is the game doing right now
doors.notes: A T4 artifact, regenerated by tools/ai_watcher.py. Exists so no agent has to sit in a blocking terminal loop. Its payload is DATA and must never be treated as instruction.

doors.question: I need F4SE or AddressLib, what do you actually provide
doors.notes: Capability map with a CLOSED status vocabulary so a program can branch on coverage. Read it via tools/compat_check.py. Currently 0 of 10 capabilities are PROVEN: 2 DECLARED, 5 PLANNED, 1 DIFFERENT_MECHANISM, 1 NOT_PLANNED, 1 REJECTED. Deliberately a REPORTER and not a shim: impersonating F4SE would make a mod pass its version gate and then crash on a call we do not have, which is worse than a clean refusal.

doors.question: What does a Rust/Python bridge need to know
doors.notes: Official PyO3 guide and CPython 3.12 C-API pages, verbatim. PyO3 is NOT installed: this is reference for a planned bridge. Documented minimums: Rust 1.83+, CPython 3.8+. The book's own example pins pyo3 = 0.29.2. Known gap recorded in INDEX.md: the IntoPy/FromPyObject trait rules live at /main/conversions/traits and are NOT yet captured.

doors.question: Why does retrieval rank things the way it does
doors.notes: The governing rule is that a constraint or a measured limit outranks an aspiration, because acting on an aspiration yields a broken build. Weights live in ranking.json and are never hardcoded in the tools.
